tip: Polite way to ask for directions.
translation_en: Excuse me, where is the train station?
How do I get to the main train station?

sentence: Gehen Sie die erste Straße rechts.
translation_en: Take the first street on the right.

sentence: Gehen Sie die zweite Straße links.
translation_en: Take the second street on the left.

tip: Separable prefix 'ab' goes to the end.

sentence: Gehen Sie an der Kirche vorbei.
Der Bahnhof ist auf der rechten Seite.
translation_en: The train station is on the right side.

sentence: Das Hotel ist auf der linken Seite.
translation_en: The hotel is on the left side.

sentence: Es ist nicht weit von hier.
translation_en: It is not far from here.

tip: 'mit' requires the dative case (der Bus -> dem Bus).

sentence: Nehmen Sie den Bus Linie vier.
Der Zug fährt um neun Uhr ab.
translation_en: The train departs at nine o'clock.

sentence: Der Zug kommt um zehn Uhr an.
translation_en: The train arrives at ten o'clock.

tip: 'umsteigen' (to transfer/change trains). Stays whole at the end because of modal verb 'müssen'.
translation_en: Where do we have to transfer?

tip: Modal verb 'müssen' pushes 'umsteigen' to the end.

sentence: Der Zug fährt auf Gleis vier ab.
translation_en: The train departs from track four.

sentence: Bitte achten Sie auf die Durchsage.
tip: 'achten auf' means to pay attention to.
translation_en: Please pay attention to the announcement.
How long does the journey take?

tip: 'im Stau' means in a traffic jam.
translation_en: We are stuck in a traffic jam.
We are visiting the old town.
We are doing a city walking tour.
The town hall is very old.
We meet at the market square.

tip: Modal verb 'dürfen' (darf) + infinitive at the end.
translation_en: Is one allowed to park here?
What is your favorite means of transport?
We are going to a rave.

sentence: Wir trinken Cocktails in der Strandbar.
translation_en: We drink cocktails in the beach bar.
We roll the dice for the win.
Thank you very much for the info.
